Re: LD 649, An Act to Certify Chiropractic Assistants Who Perform X-rays as Radiologic Technologists
Dear Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and Members of the Committee:
I am writing on behalf of the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation's Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation ("OPOR"), an umbrella agency that supports the Maine Board of Chiropractic Licensure ("Board").
This bill creates a new licensure category within the Board of Chiropractic Licensure ("Board") establishing the requirements for a licensed chiropractic assistant to obtain a radiologic technology certification to use ionizing radiation as part of their duties while working in a chiropractic office. It requires the Board to determine the minimum qualifications for the certification, including completion of a Board-approved radiologic technology course and to adopt continuing professional education rules for licensure renewal.
OPOR is not taking a position on LD 649, but offers the following information as the Committee considers the necessity of this bill:
1. Is this level of regulation necessary to protect the public when seeking chiropractic services? No, not necessarily. Under the current practice act, a chiropractor may delegate certain duties to a licensed chiropractic assistant so long as they are under the direct control of and in the presence of the chiropractor. The chiropractor delegating those activities is legally liable for those activities performed by such an individual and that individual is considered to be the chiropractor's agent.
2. See Title 32, Chapter 9 Chiropractors. However, existing laws governing the practice of radiologic technology prevent such delegation as there is not a stated exemption for licensed chiropractic assistants. Testimony ofRep. Nathan Wadsworth introducing
LD 649, "An Act to Certify Chiropractic Assistants Who Perform X-rays as
Radiologic Technologists " Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance,
and Financial Services
March 13, 2025
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance, and Financial Services;
My name is Representative Nathan Wadsworth and I represent House District 82, which
includes the towns of Brownfield, Fryeburg, Lovell, Hiram, and Porter. I am here today
to introduce LD 649, "An Act to Certify Chiropractic Assistants Who Perform X-
rays as Radiologic Technologists" . This legislation is a critical step toward improving patient access to timely imaging services while maintaining high standards of care.
Under current regulations, patients in need of diagnostic X-rays often face unnecessary
delays, particularly those who must visit hospitals or imaging centers. These facilities are
frequently overburdened, leading to long wait times that can delay treatment and prolong
patient discomfort. By certifying chiropractic assistants to perform X-rays as radiologic
technologists, this bill offers a practical solution----alloWing patients to receive necessary imaging services directly in chiropractic offices without long hospital wait times. This legislation establishes rigorous certification requirements to ensure safety and competency. Chiropractic assistants seeking certification must:
o Hold a valid license under section 556. 0 Complete a board-approved course with at least 50 hours of instruction, covering
critical areas such as radiographic equipment, exposure principles, radiation protection, anatomy, and positioning. - Pass a proficiency examination in radiologic technology. - Pay a certification fee not exceeding $100, ensuring affordability for practitioners.
By meeting these standards, chiropractic assistants will be well-equipped to produce
high-quality diagnostic images while ensuring patient safety. Additionally, the bill mandates continuing, education for certificate renewal, keeping practitioners updated on
best practices.

Allowing trained chiropractic assistants to perfonn X-rays will significantly improve efficiency in healthcare delivery. Instead of waiting hours or even days for hospital imaging, patients can access necessary X-rays in a familiar, convenient setting--reducing overall system strain and expediting care. Furthermore, requiring visible display of certification in chiropractic offices ensures transparency and patient confidence. I urge the Committee to support this legislation, which will expand patient access, alleviate hospital burdens, and maintain high radiologic safety standards. Thank you for your time and consideration. Nathan J. Wadsworth

MCA MAINE CHIROPRACTIC AESOCIAYION

To: Maine Legislature Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services
Date: March 11, 2025
Re: LD 649 An Act To Certify Chiropractic Assistants Who perform X-Rays as Radiologic
Technicians, Sponsored by Representative Wadsworth
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson and distinguished members of the Committee on
Health Coverage, insurance and Financial Services. My name is Robert Reed, l am the Executive Director of the Maine Chiropractic Association (MCA) testifying on behalf of my employer. The MCA represents over two hundred Chiropractic Doctors, their staff and most importantly, the patients they serve. We present today offering our support for this bill.
LD 649 will allow a Certified Chiropractic Assistant to hold an additional certification allowing that individual to produce x-rays in a Chiropractic office. Our leadership has reviewed the training requirements presented in the bill and have great respect for the American Chiropractic Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ACRRT), which is a subchapter of the
American Board of Chiropractic Radiology. The MCA believes their training program provides
acceptable training for the limited number of x-ray services performed in a Chiropractic setting
and is already established and allowed in several other states.
In addition, because the added certification requires they be a Certified Chiropractic Assistant with requirements previously approved by the Legislature and administered by the Maine Chiropractic Board of Licensing, these individuals will already possess 36 hours of training including anatomy, physiology, and chiropractic methodologies. That primary certification allows Chiropractic staff to provide or assist with services that are then reimbursed by
insurance carriers.
This model provides the training we believe is necessary by utilizing a nationally recognized board program and has verifiable testing of skills and as such we ask for your consideration in
approving this bill.
We thank the Committee for its time and energy and stand ready to provide answers to any
questions you may have of the Association.
